questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate the difference between India’s share of world exports of rice in 2010 and 2022. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Which one of the following would not be classified by an economist as a factor of production?
options: Labour temporarily out of work
Money in a firm’s bank account
Non-agricultural land
Risk-taking entrepreneurs

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 1 and Figure 2) show that the rice export ban by India in 2022 is likely to have had a significant impact on the world price of rice.

The central purpose of economic activity is the production of goods and services to satisfy needs and wants. Which of the following is one of the three key decisions that has to be taken to achieve this?
options: How to achieve economies of scale
What goods and services to produce
Where to locate businesses
Whether to maximise profit or sales

questions.questionText: Extract B (line 19) states: ‘In Nigeria, the demand for rice is very price inelastic’. With the help of a diagram, explain how the Indian export ban is likely to have affected the market for rice in Nigeria.
Figure 1 shows the market demand for electric cars. The shift of the market demand curve from D1 to D2 would most likely be caused by
options: a fall in the price of electric cars.
a government subsidy to producers of electric cars.
a marketing campaign promoting electric cars.
a reduction in the price of petrol and diesel fuels.

questions.questionText: Extract C (lines 6–7) states: ‘An alternative would be to impose a maximum price for consumers, as both Sri Lanka and the Philippines have done’. Using the data and your knowledge of economics, evaluate the view that imposing a maximum price for rice is the best way for a rice-importing nation, such as Nigeria, to ensure the affordability of a basic food for its citizens.
A firm hopes to increase its market share by setting its prices lower than most of its competitors. What is the most likely reason for this strategy?
options: The firm has a licence that gives it a temporary monopoly
The firm is a price taker in a very competitive market
The firm is aiming to differentiate its products from its competitors
The firm is aiming to increase its long-run profits

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the median number of storm overflow hours by water company in 2022.

A firm allows customers to personalise a mug with a name of their choice, which it sells for £15. The firm pays £3 for each mug. The paint and labour cost an extra £7. The firm has fixed costs of £150 per month and in a typical month, it produces and sells 60 mugs. What is the average cost of producing one personalised mug?
Explain how the data in Extract D (Figure 4) show that household water bills have increased in real terms since privatisation in 1989.
One reason why merit goods, such as education and health care, can lead to market failure is that
options: individuals are unwilling to pay for merit goods.
individuals have incomplete information about merit goods.
merit goods are generally provided free by the government.
merit goods are subject to the free-rider problem.

questions.questionText: Extract E (line 10) states: ‘The minimum efficient scale in the water industry is large’. With the help of a diagram, explain why the large minimum efficient scale in the water industry is likely to lead to the market being supplied by a few large firms with monopoly power.
Figure 2 shows the market for a good. S1 shows the supply if only private costs are considered and S2 shows the supply if social costs are taken into account. At the free market output, there is
options: a negative externality and overproduction of the good.
a negative externality and underproduction of the good.
a positive externality and overproduction of the good.
a positive externality and underproduction of the good.

questions.questionText: Extract F (lines 5–6) states: ‘if regulators impose fines, these costs may be passed on to consumers or reduce investment’. Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that stronger regulation would be a better policy than bringing the water industry back into public ownership.

Microchips are used in a wide range of products, including mobile phones and traffic lights. If demand increases for one of these products, this affects the price of other products that need microchips. This is an example of
options: complementary goods.
composite demand.
joint supply.
substitute goods.

questions.questionText: Explain, with examples, the differences between a private good, a public good and a quasi-public good.
A firm uses a variety of strategies to improve its market position. Which one of the following strategies is most likely to benefit consumers in the long run?
options: An advertising campaign that promotes the product’s image
Charging low prices to drive rival firms out of the market
Investing in research and development to improve product quality
Merging with a rival to reduce competition in the market

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that oligopolies serve society well.
Table 1 shows the percentage market share of firms in a particular industry in 2020 and 2023. What was the change in the three-firm concentration ratio over the period 2020 to 2023?
options: A fall of 6 percentage points
A fall of 7 percentage points
A rise of 4 percentage points
A rise of 5 percentage points

questions.questionText: Explain how technological progress can affect productivity, efficiency and firms’ costs of production.
All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to result in a fall in the market price of rice?
options: Farmers releasing less rice for sale
Good weather conditions for growing rice
More wheat being planted instead of rice
The removal of a subsidy for growing rice

questions.questionText: Assess the view that the main objective of firms is to maximise profits.
Which one of the following is most likely to influence the price elasticity of supply of a good or service?
options: The availability of spare capacity
The number of substitutes for the product
The percentage of income spent on the good
The price of complementary goods

questions.questionText: Explain the factors that determine a firm’s demand for labour.

In Figure 3, the curve XX shows the initial production possibility boundary (PPB) for a toy manufacturer producing trains and buses. Which one of the following combinations is most likely to explain why the firm’s PPB has shifted from XX to YY?
Assess the view that a national minimum wage, such as the UK’s National Living Wage, contributes to an improvement in economic welfare.
Which one of the following is the best example of a situation where there is asymmetric information?
options: A firm operating in perfect competition
A seller knowing more than a buyer
Two buyers being equally informed
Two firms working together on a new product

questions.questionText: Table 2 shows the weekly demand for two products, apples and pears, before and after a change in the price of pears. What is the cross elasticity of demand for apples following the change in the price of pears?

Developed economies, such as the UK, are characterised by high levels of specialisation which involve workers concentrating on a specific task or occupation. This specialisation is possible because in such economies
options: an effective medium of exchange exists.
markets tend to have high levels of concentration.
production is concentrated in the service sector.
production tends to involve mainly unskilled labour.

questions.questionText: Figure 4, shows the original demand (D1) and supply (S) in the market for jewellery. D2 shows the demand after an increase in incomes. After the increase in incomes, the market price of jewellery will rise due to
options: excess demand at price P1.
excess supply at price P1.
increased average cost of producing jewellery.
increased competition between sellers.

questions.questionText: Following a period of unusually cold weather, growers find that many of their tomato plants have been destroyed, reducing the supply of tomatoes. As a result of this
options: the price of tomatoes falls due to the signalling function of prices.
the price of tomatoes rises due to the rationing function of prices.
the quantity of tomatoes demanded rises due to the incentive function of prices.
the supply of tomatoes will fall further due to the signalling function of prices.

questions.questionText: Table 3 shows indices for the total revenue and total cost for a firm in the years 2021 to 2023, with 2022 set as the base year. In 2021, the firm’s total revenue was £180 000 and its total cost was £160 000. What was the firm’s total profit in 2023?
Which one of the following is an example of government failure due to unintended consequences?
options: A government target to increase police officers is missed due to a low number of applicants
Government provision of a free flu vaccine for the over 60s has a low take-up
The government cancels a plan for a new railway line after an expensive planning enquiry
The government introduces a charge at a waste disposal site which leads to illegal dumping

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1), calculate how the value of the Norwegian krone has changed compared to the Singapore dollar between 26 October 2021 and 29 May 2023. Give your answer as a percentage and to one decimal place.
Which one of the following is most likely to be an objective of government macroeconomic policy?
options: Achieving deflation in the average price level
Creating a budget surplus during a recession
Generating stable and sustained economic growth
Improving productivity in an electronics firm

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that Singapore may have benefitted from managing its exchange rate compared to Germany and Norway.
In an economy, the number of people in work is unchanged but the rate of growth of labour productivity slows from 2.3% to 0.4%. It can be concluded that there will be an increase in
options: cyclical unemployment.
national income.
raw material prices.
the negative output gap.

questions.questionText: Extract B (lines 6–7) states: ‘Some analysts hope that, before long, the currency will start to appreciate which could help Norway reduce inflation.’ With the help of a suitable diagram, explain how an appreciation of the krone could help Norway reduce inflation.
In a particular year, the rate of inflation in an economy was 2% and real national income rose by 6%. What was the approximate increase in the economy’s nominal national income in that year?

Extract C (lines 1–2) states: ‘An economy that has seen considerable success by intervening in the foreign exchange market to manage its currency is Singapore.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that an economy is likely to perform better with a managed exchange rate rather than a freely floating exchange rate.

Figure 1 shows the aggregate demand (AD) and long-run aggregate supply (LRAS) curves for an economy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is most likely to cause aggregate demand to shift from AD1 to AD2 and long-run aggregate supply to shift from LRAS1 to LRAS2?
options: A fall in spending on imports and a rise in productivity
A reduction in exports and an increase in imports of capital goods
An increase in Bank Rate and a reduction in firms’ costs of production
An increase in saving and a rise in government spending on infrastructure

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the difference between the percentage increase in GDP for Japan and the USA between 2001 and 2023. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Which one of the following statements concerning short-run economic growth and long-run economic growth is correct?
options: Short-run growth is inflationary whereas long-run growth will cause a fall in the average price level
Short-run growth may occur independently of the government whereas long-run growth is only achieved as a result of government policy
Short-run growth may occur when governments use demand-side policies but these do not affect long-run growth
Short-run growth may reduce spare capacity whereas long-run growth increases productive capacity

questions.questionText: Explain how the data in Extract D (Figure 3) show how Ethiopia has developed at a faster rate than Japan since 2001.
When an economy goes into a recession, there is most likely to be an increase in
options: business uncertainty.
imports.
inflation.
tax revenue.

questions.questionText: Extract E (lines 15–17) states: ‘In recent years, some of the BRICS+ countries, including China and India, have been responsible for large foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows into the G7.’ With the help of a suitable diagram, explain how increased inward foreign direct investment (FDI) can affect a country’s level of employment.
Table 1 shows the levels of government spending and national income in a country in Year 1 and Year 2. All other things being equal, what is the value of the multiplier to two decimal places?

Extract F (lines 1–2) states: ‘While some see the benefits of the emergence of the BRICS+ economies, others are more worried by their rapid economic growth.’ Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess the view that the continued rapid economic growth of the BRICS+ economies is likely to be damaging to the macroeconomic performance of G7 nations, such as the UK.
Which one of the following is most likely to cause a leftward shift in the short-run aggregate supply curve?
options: A reduction in the national minimum wage
A rise in the general price level
A rise in the price of imported raw materials
An increase in government subsidies to firms

questions.questionText: Explain factors that may lead to an increase in a country’s national debt as a percentage of GDP.
Table 2 shows various macroeconomic indicators for an economy from 2021 to 2023. Which one of the following can be concluded from the data in Table 2?
options: Incomes are more equitably distributed due to lower unemployment
The central bank should reduce interest rates
The government’s budget deficit has increased
There is evidence of a conflict between macroeconomic policy objectives

questions.questionText: Assess the view that raising direct taxes to finance an increase in government spending is better than raising indirect taxes.
Which one of the following combinations consists only of injections into the circular flow of income?
options: Consumption, bank loans, investment
Exports, government spending, investment
Government spending, consumption, exports
Investment, bank loans, exports

questions.questionText: Explain how supply-side policies can help to achieve a low, stable rate of inflation.
Figure 2 shows a production possibility curve for an economy producing consumer and capital goods. The movement from point X to point Y is most likely to have been caused by
options: a fall in the exchange rate.
a fall in the trade surplus.
a rise in the foreign currency price of exports.
a rise in the volume of imports.

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that a low rate of inflation is always beneficial for a country’s macroeconomic performance.
Which one of the following statements about supply-side policies is correct? Supply-side policies
options: have no effect on aggregate demand.
often rely on creating economic incentives.
only affect long-run aggregate supply.
usually lead to an increase in inflation.

questions.questionText: Explain the main limitations of using national income data to assess differences in living standards between countries.
Which one of the following is the most likely reason for a fall in saving by households?
options: A reduction in consumer confidence

households completing business surveys to reveal their preferred products.
firms planning their activities to meet production targets set by government.
entrepreneurs producing their own goods to satisfy their own needs and wants.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows a production possibility boundary for an economy that produces goods and services. From the diagram it can be concluded that
options: point X is productively efficient and point Y is allocatively efficient.
point Y is productively efficient and point X is allocatively efficient.
points X and Y are allocatively efficient.
points X and Y are productively efficient.

questions.questionText: A demand curve is drawn on the assumption that
options: quantity demanded always increases as price falls.
changes in price do not influence supply.
price elasticity of demand does not vary along the demand curve.
factors affecting demand, other than price, remain constant.

questions.questionText: Monopoly can provide an example of market failure because firms with monopoly power
options: may produce a larger output than would be supplied in a competitive market so that they achieve economies of scale.
may produce a lower output, less efficiently, than would be supplied by a competitive market.
always charge high prices and earn high profits.
have no incentive to meet consumer demands.

questions.questionText: The cross elasticity of demand between goods X and Y is positive. This implies that they are
options: normal goods.
substitute goods.
goods in composite demand.
complementary goods.

questions.questionText: Many agricultural products are subject to large fluctuations in price. One reason why these large fluctuations occur is because the
options: demand for agricultural products is income inelastic in the long run.
supply of agricultural products is price elastic in the long run.
supply of agricultural products is price inelastic in the short run.
demand for agricultural products is price elastic in the short run.

questions.questionText: A good has a price elasticity of supply of +0.8. At present, the quantity supplied of the good is 200 units per week at a market price of £800 per unit. If the price rises to £1000 per unit then the quantity supplied per week would
options: increase to 250 units.
increase to 240 units.
increase to 360 units.
decrease to 160 units.

questions.questionText: A reduction in the market price of a firm’s product will always result in an increase in its profits or a reduction in its losses if it
options: increases its share of the market.
increases its total revenue by more than its total costs.
enables it to reduce its average costs.
leads to a reduction in the price of its inputs.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows a firm’s average total cost curve (ATC), with the firm producing an output of OX. The firm’s productive efficiency will improve if the
options: ATC curve shifts upwards for any given level of output.
ATC curve shifts downwards for any given level of output.
firm increases its level of output.
firm reduces its level of output.

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, which one of the following situations always results in a rise in labour productivity?
options: Output falls at a slower rate than the fall in the number of workers employed
Output falls at a faster rate than the fall in the number of workers employed
Output rises at a slower rate than the rise in the number of workers employed
Output always rises as the number of workers employed increases

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the best indicator of the degree of competition in an industry?
options: The industry’s concentration ratio
The elasticity of supply of the industry’s output
The number of workers employed in the industry
The total value of the industry’s sales

options: public goods are of equal benefit to all consumers.
there is no opportunity cost in the provision of public goods.
people could consume the good without paying for it.
the government should not levy a tax for providing public goods.

questions.questionText: The elasticity of supply of a particular good is more likely to be low
options: the shorter the time period under consideration.
if the good in question has many close substitutes.
if the good in question is a necessity.
if complementary goods are required for its consumption.

questions.questionText: The diagram below illustrates a market in which a monopolist takes control and sets a price above the competitive level. The price charged by the monopolist is OS. options: RSTY.
OS multiplied by OW.
RSTU.
RSTY minus WYUV.

questions.questionText: An increase in the world market price of wheat, following a series of poor harvests, leading to falling sales is an example of
options: market failure due to an externality in production.
government failure to support agricultural markets.
scarcity caused by high prices.
the rationing function of price.

options: vertical distance FE2.
increase in price P1P2.
the diagonal distance E1E2.
the horizontal distance GE1.

The diagram shows the market for
options: a merit good.
a public good.
a good with negative externalities in production.
a good with positive externalities in production.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statements about the distribution of income must be correct?
options: The distribution of income is equitable when everyone has the same income
‘The distribution of income is equitable’ is a positive statement
An unequal distribution of income is, by definition, inequitable
Whether the distribution of income is equitable depends on a value judgement

questions.questionText: Changes in real GDP are used to measure
options: inflation.
the level of employment.
economic growth.
the distribution of income.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows two aggregate demand curves (AD) for an economy. All other things being equal, the most likely cause of the shift from AD1 to AD2 is an increase in
options: exports.
the rate of inflation.
interest rates.
the budget deficit.

questions.questionText: All other things being equal, the long-run aggregate supply curve of an economy is likely to shift to the right if there is an increase in
options: factor mobility.
raw material prices.
indirect taxation.
wage rates.

questions.questionText: A country has a slow rate of growth of productivity and rising cyclical unemployment. All other things being equal, which measures are most likely to increase the rate of growth of productivity and reduce cyclical unemployment?
options: Increased investment and increased saving
More government spending on training and a higher exchange rate
Decreased benefit payments and a lower budget deficit
Lower taxation on firms and lower interest rates

options: A decrease in imports
An increase in savings
A decrease in the money supply
An increase in productivity

Between 2011 and 2013, GDP grew by 8% whereas population grew by 3%

Money GDP increased by more than real GDP between 2011 and 2015

UK firms do not have sufficient productive capacity to satisfy customer demand
The skills possessed by UK workers do not match those which are required by UK employers

questions.questionText: Structural unemployment is most likely to occur because of
options: labour being temporarily unemployed when moving between jobs.
fluctuations in the level of aggregate demand.
the seasonal nature of certain occupations.
long-term changes in the pattern of demand for the products of particular industries.

questions.questionText: An economy is in macroeconomic equilibrium, producing at its normal capacity level of output. Without long-run economic growth, a persistent increase in aggregate demand is likely to lead to an increase in the level of
options: real GDP.
employment.
productivity.
prices.

the primary income (income flows) balance must be positive.
the combined primary and secondary income (income flows and transfers) balance must be positive.
the value of services exported must exceed the value of goods imported.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is an example of contractionary fiscal policy?
options: Decreasing the supply of credit
Increasing spending on welfare benefits
Reducing progressive taxation
Increasing the size of the budget surplus

options: surplus on the current account of the balance of payments.
price of imported goods.
level of unemployment.
rate of economic growth.

questions.questionText: A budget deficit is most likely to occur when
options: the value of imports exceeds the value of exports.
government spending exceeds tax revenue.
the volume of imports exceeds the volume of exports.
direct and indirect taxes are reduced.

options: In 2013, the economy’s negative output gap increased.
In 2014, the amount of spare capacity in the economy increased.

options: Supply-side improvements in the economy can only be brought about by government policy.
Supply-side policies are intended to increase the long-run trend rate of economic growth.
Supply-side policies are designed to reduce the size of a negative output gap.
Supply-side policies ensure increased capacity utilisation in the economy.

Income = Output = Injections
Output = Expenditure = Withdrawals
